results.evidence: The test writes a Latin-1 byte (\xe9) migration file and runs main(['migrate','--db',...]). It asserts the return is EXIT_REFUSED, which is 1 (cottonwood/cli.py:40). It also asserts stderr starts with 'error: ', contains '001_latin1.sql', and has no 'Traceback'. db._apply now turns UnicodeDecodeError into MigrationError, and the cli prints that as 'error: ...'. All 3 tests in the file passed on pytest.

test_no_transaction_is_left_open_after_a_failed_migration applies a migration containing invalid SQL (NOT SQL) through db._apply on an autocommit connection. It expects MigrationError and asserts conn.in_transaction is False, user_version is 0 and no tables remain. _apply rolls back if conn.in_transaction on sqlite3.Error. The run of tests/test_apply_error_branches.py gave 3 passed. I did not run a mutant check, so I have not shown that the test fails if the rollback is removed.

results.evidence: tests/test_apply_error_branches.py::test_version_prints_the_package_version asserts main(["--version"]) == EXIT_OK and captured stdout == "cottonwood 0.1.0\n". I did not check that EXIT_OK is 0; it is imported from cottonwood.cli. The CLI defines --version as action=version with version=f"cottonwood {__version__}" (cottonwood/cli.py:1529), and __version__ = "0.1.0" (cottonwood/__init__.py:3). The run `uv run --offline pytest -q tests/test_apply_error_branches.py -v` passed 3 of 3 tests. Two things could make this less direct. I read the test and source in the ccge-008 worktree, but the session's primary directory is ccge-006. I did not run a mutation probe.
